newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-KENT LEADS GIANTS PAST PIRATES.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-KENT LEADS GIANTS PAST PIRATES.

text.p: Newly acquired Jeff Kent helped San Franciso fans get over the loss of slugger Matt Williams when he powered the Giants to a 7-5 win over the Pittsburgh Pirates on Thursday.
Kent, acquired along with shortstop Jose Vizcaino and pitcher Julian Tavarez in a deal that sent Williams to Cleveland, homered, doubled and had five RBI.
Kent hit a two-run homer to left-centre off Pittsburgh starter and loser Steve Cooke in the first inning as the Giants jumped out to a 3-0 lead.

The Pirates intentionally walked Barry Bonds to load the bases in the fourth inning. But Kent foiled the strategy with a double that scored Darryl Hamilton and Glenallen Hill to increas the Giants' lead to 6-0.
Kent added a sacrifice fly for an insurance run in the eighth.
"You have to credit the Giants," Pittsburgh manager Gene Lamont said. "They jumped on us pretty quickly and it's tough to come back when you're down six."
Osvaldo Fernandez got the win desite surrendering Mark Johnson's grand slam in the fifth inning.
In Montreal, Rondell White, Shane Andrews and David Segui each hit two-run homers to lead the Expos to a 9-4 win and a sweep of the three-game season-opening series with the St Louis Cardinals.
Carlos Perez, who was sidelined the entire 1996 season with arm problems, went seven innings, allowing four runs and seven hits.

White's homer in the fourth off Cardinals starter and loser Alan Benes knotted the score 4-4. Segui gave the Expos a 7-4 lead with his homer in the fifth and Andrews capped the scoring with his blast off Tony Fossas in the seventh.

In Cincinnati, Larry Walker had an RBI double and a run-scoring single in a six-run fourth inning and Mark Thompson pitched seven scoreless innings as the Colorado Rockies pounded the Reds 7-1 for their first win.
Walker also hit a solo homer in the seventh for the Rockies.

Thompson, who threw 65 of his 109 pitches for strikes, gave up five hits with one walk and three strikeouts as the Rockies limited the Reds to one run after giving up 16 runs in the first two games of the series.

In Houston, Jeff Blauser and Keith Lockhart had sacrifice flies in the eighth inning as the Atlanta Braves -- held to no hits over 6 2/3 innings by Darryl Kile -- rallied for a 3-2 win over the Astros to avert a three-game sweep.
Tom Glavine got the win, allowing six hits over seven innings. He left trailing 2-1 but got the win as Atlanta rallied in the eighth off Kile.
Kile took a no hitter into the seventh. But Fred McGriff hit a 2-1 pitch over the centre-field for Atlanta's first run.
At Florida, Alex Fernandez allowed one run over 6 2/3 innings and Jeff Conine hit a grand slam to lead the Marlins to an 8-2 win over the Chicago Cubs and a sweep of their three-game series.

Fernandez, who spent seven seasons with the Chicago White Sox before signing a five-year, $35 million contract with the Marlins in the off-season, allowed five hits and struck out two in his first National League start.
Moises Alou had three hits and two RBI for the Marlins, who opened a season 3-0 for the first time.
In Los Angeles, Ismael Valdes allowed one run over seven innings and Mike Piazza homered as the Dodgers nipped the Philadelphia Phillies 2-1 in the rubber game of a three-game series.
Valdes allowed five hits, walked one and struck out four for the win. Philadelphia's Mark Leiter pitched six innings, allowing two runs and seven hits for the loss.
Piazza led off the sixth inning with a solo blast and Todd Hollandsworth's double to left scored Eric Karros with the game-winning run.
In San Diego, Bobby Jones allowed six hits over eight innings and Bernard Gilkey smacked a two-run homer as the New York Mets beat the Padres 4-1 for their first win.
Jones walked just one and struck out six before giving way in the ninth to John Franco, who bounced back from a blown save Wednesday, tossing a scoreless frame for the save.
Jones retired 10 straight batters between the second and fifth and allowed just three singles over his final 6 2/3 innings.
Fernando Valenzuela was tagged for four runs for the loss.
